attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, presented as his own analysis.

semantics.note: Keeps the $2T threshold, the 'brand new' and AI-specific scope, the 'by 2030' horizon and the 'based on my analysis' basis. 'Needs to ... or all of this was for nothing' reads as a conditional: if revenue falls short, the spending was wasted.

contract.note: Reading 'for nothing' as failed economic payback, and limiting big tech to the four firms named just before, is an ordinary reading. The contract correctly leaves annual vs cumulative revenue open, and the deadline is not changed.

evidence.note: Bain's Sept 2025 estimate of $2T a year in new revenue needed for 2030 compute. It is a similar analyst scenario, not evidence of actual revenue or payback for the four firms.

reviews.rationale: The deadline (end of 2030) is after the 2026-10-28 evaluation date, and no conclusive event meets the early-resolution rule. We can't yet know whether the revenue condition will fail, and the packet has no payback evidence. The Bain item is context only.

attribution.note: Zitron restates and defends his own earlier reporting in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: An estimate of past revenue that keeps its stated basis (extrapolated from the 20% share). 'Suggests' marks where the figure came from, but he states the number firmly and defends it, so this is a testable claim about the past, not a probability.

contract.note: Reading the period as Jan–Sep 2025 and the measure as total booked revenue follows from his calendar-year context and his accrual-accounting remarks. The rounding interval is strict, but a contradiction would require a materially different total.

evidence.note: TechCrunch's source says the leaked payments are Microsoft's net share, so the extrapolation likely understates revenue. It does not put a number on the gap or give an independent nine-month total. The cited first-half figure covers a different period.

reviews.rationale: No independent Jan–Sep 2025 revenue total is in the packet. TechCrunch raises a credible objection that the figure is net, not gross, but gives no reconciled number. The first-half figure it mentions is another period, so it is context only. The evidence does not settle the claim either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own estimate, in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: Keeps 'I estimate', the AI-only capex and the brand-new-revenue scope. The claim is a modelled revenue requirement with no recovery period, margin or cost assumptions, so no observed outcome could confirm or refute it.

contract.note: The contract adds a Q3 2025 reference period, recovery assumptions and margin requirements that the speaker never gave. Any result would depend on the evaluator's choices, not on his words.

evidence.note: Sequoia's 2024 model of ecosystem revenue needs uses its own assumptions. It covers a different period and population and does not test the four-firm ratio.
Microsoft's own disclosure of $34.9B capex for cloud and AI. It gives no AI-only base or margin, so it cannot test the ratio.

reviews.rationale: 'Needs $2 for every $1 of capex' is a modelled requirement with no recovery period, margin or cost basis. No dated evidence could show it true or false without supplying those assumptions, which the speaker never gave. It is untestable as stated. Both evidence items are context only.

attribution.note: The $5B full-year estimate is Zitron's own. The $833M December figure is attributed to Anthropic and correctly left out.

semantics.note: 'Will end up having $5 billion' is a firm forecast. 'Based on my estimates' gives his basis, not a probability hedge, so the claim is scored. The horizon is calendar year 2025.

contract.note: A round '$5 billion' fairly means the nearest billion ($4.5B–$5.5B), an ordinary rounding reading. The demand to reconcile the gross/net basis is stricter than the plain words: he gave no basis, so audited reported revenue is the ordinary measure.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1, filed 2026-10-26 (before the evaluation date), reports audited 2025 revenue of $4.585B for the full calendar year. That is inside the $4.5B–$5.5B interval. Ordinary reported revenue matches the unspecified metric in the claim.

reviews.rationale: The horizon ended 2025-12-31. Audited 2025 revenue of $4.585B rounds to the forecast $5B. The speaker named no net basis, so reported GAAP revenue is the plain measure, not a different accounting basis. On the stricter exact-minimum reading ($5B or more) the forecast would miss; the rounding reading is the fair one.
